page: Microsoft Azure E96as_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EASv4 server family. It is powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture. The server features 96 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 48 physical cores with multithreading enabled. It is equipped with 672.0 GB of system memory, providing 7.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. Local storage consists of a 1376 GB SSD, and the instance is Premium Storage capable. The virtualization layer is managed by the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor.

In benchmark evaluations, the E96as_v4 demonstrates strong multi-core capabilities, placing in the top 10% for stress-ng multi-core CPU performance and the top 10% for PassMark CPU encryption tests. Single-core performance is also strong, ranking in the top 25% for stress-ng single-core tests. Memory subsystem performance is highlighted by a top-tier PassMark memory score and strong cached read-only memory bandwidth, though uncached large-block read and write operations perform at average levels. Cryptographic and integer operations benefit from hardware-accelerated instruction sets, including AES, VAES, and SHA_NI.

This server configuration is designed for memory-intensive workloads that require high core counts and substantial memory capacity without dedicated GPU acceleration. The high density of RAM relative to vCPUs makes it highly cost-efficient for large-scale database deployments, in-memory caching systems like Redis, and multi-threaded data decompression tasks. It is also well-suited for software compilation, ray tracing, and medium-scale language model inference where CPU-based execution is preferred over GPU-based setups.
